rationale: All candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm, but PGS001784 is the only one reporting a clearly PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R² with covariates regressed out = 0.0147) in a large European validation (n=350,767) with only basic demographic/PC covariates. Alternatives either lack PRS-only metrics (PGS002054 reports only partial-r; PGS000753 only OR per SD=1.37 with very low variant count; PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973 report full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown or covariate-inflated settings), making their discrimination evidence less comparable for ranking.

PGS002738 is the only candidate whose reported trait/phenotype is directly alcohol use disorder with trait_efo alcohol dependence, aligning best to the target alcohol dependence, and it shows a reasonably strong PRS effect (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96) in a sizable European validation (n=7,900). Competing scores (PGS000201/PGS000202) are for problematic alcohol use with only small incremental ΔR² (0.0119/0.0046) on a criteria-count phenotype, and PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American cohorts, making it less directly applicable when ancestry is unspecified.

All three candidates are direct matches by trait_efo/phenotyping. PGS004913 is a disease-focused PRS for alcohol-associated cirrhosis with explicit PRS contribution reported (R²=0.029) and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), whereas PGS000704 and PGS001777 report only full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) without PRS-only metrics and thus are less comparable as standalone PGSs; PGS000704’s HR per SD is modest (1.18). The heritability lookup is noisy/low-match, so it does not strongly arbitrate among candidates.

All candidates are direct matches for angina pectoris, but PGS001262 provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.5868; PGS R² 0.0130) with only basic covariates and the largest PRS-only AUROC/R² among the UKB snpnet angina endpoints. Several newer ICD10/PheCode scores report only full-model C-index or per-SD OR without PRS-only metrics, making them less comparable; the PGS001262 PRS-only R² is also consistent with the low observed h² (~0.01–0.02) for angina in UKB.

All candidates are direct matches for ankylosing spondylitis, but PGS001268 provides explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics with basic covariates and large UKB training/European validation, whereas the portability-framework scores (PGS001876/PGS002089) report only partial-r and the East Asian study scores report only full-model AUC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298). Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001268 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R² than PGS001267, with otherwise identical design; the time-to-event endpoint is a mild endpoint-fidelity caveat, so confidence is moderate.

PGS005254 is a direct-match aortic stenosis score with a large reported training sample (n=205,483), genome-wide PRS-CS construction (~1.11M variants), and basic covariate adjustment (age/age^2/sex/PCs), supporting cleaner interpretation than covariate-heavy models. PGS005252 is also direct-match but has much smaller training (n=47,691) and reports only a covariate-augmented C-index (0.87) with many clinical predictors, making its discrimination less attributable to the PRS itself. Other candidates target hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or valve-function measurements rather than aortic stenosis.

PGS001135 is the only candidate whose trait_efo directly matches the target (arthritis) and it reports PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.539 and PGS R2 0.00291) with basic covariates, making it the most comparable standalone arthritis score. Its PRS-only R2 is well below available arthritis-related h2 estimates, and while discrimination is modest, alternative candidates are for specific arthritis subtypes (e.g., RA, OA, JIA) or report only full-model AUC with unclear covariate packaging.

PGS001344 is a direct-match asthma score with a clear diagnosis endpoint ("Asthma diagnosed by doctor"), large UKB training (n=216,121), and explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no-covariates 0.6457; PGS R2 0.0597) using only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). Its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to EUR asthma h2 estimates (~0.05–0.19 depending on scale/source), and it outperforms other direct-match candidates that either lack PRS-only metrics, use heavy covariate packaging, or show weaker incremental/partial-correlation evidence.

Among direct atopic-dermatitis/eczema candidates, PGS002755 is a genome-wide PRS-CS score (1,090,702 variants) with very large European validation (n=337,910) and a reported PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS=1.249), making it the strongest-supported standalone PRS evidence in the list. PGS001773’s very high AUROC/R² are full-model metrics (not PGS-only) from a small validation (n=676) and thus are not comparable as PRS performance, while the paradoxical-eczema-in-psoriasis scores (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) have endpoint mismatch for generic atopic eczema.

PGS001340 is a direct-match atrial fibrillation score with explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.613; PGS R2 no covariates 0.0233) and basic covariate adjustment, making it more comparable than candidates reporting only full-model AUC/C-index. Its training size (n=269,704) and multi-ancestry evaluation support portability, and the PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to AF h2 (~0.02–0.03 observed scale), whereas several newer high full-model C-indices likely reflect covariate packaging (e.g., inclusion of clinical risk factors such as CHARGE-AF).

PGS001263 is the only candidate with a direct atrial flutter endpoint across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported and it reports explicit PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.617; PGS R² 0.025) with only basic covariates. Competing scores target the broader atrial fibrillation+flutter phenotype (one is time-to-event) and/or lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R², making them less directly supported for atrial flutter despite similar UKB-based development.

PGS000327 has clean endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is autism spectrum disorder) and a disease-focused multi-cohort training set with EUR-only development/evaluation; it also reports a moderate per-SD OR=1.33 and R²=0.0245 in validation (n=7,148) with only basic covariates (PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 has an endpoint mismatch signal (phenotyping_reported: psychiatric behavior/withdrawn) and only a modest partial R² (~0.0055) with smaller validation (n=2,198), making it less directly supported for ASD despite a more complex method/variant count.

All candidates are direct matches for basal cell carcinoma, but none report PRS-only AUC/R²; most metrics are full-model AUROC with only basic covariates, limiting comparability. Within the large 2020 Cancer PRSweb sibling set (same covariates/ancestry/validation N), PGS000452 shows the strongest effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.66; top-1% vs rest OR 3.61) with high full-model AUROC (0.632), making it the best-supported choice despite modest training N and lack of PRS-only metrics.

All candidates are direct matches to bilirubin metabolism disease, but PGS000924 uses a time-to-event endpoint and reports unusually high PRS-only AUROC/R² (0.887/0.218) that is hard to reconcile with available bilirubin-related h² estimates (~0.01–0.09), suggesting non-comparable reporting or optimism. Between the two portability-study scores with the cleanest endpoint (disorders of bilirubin excretion), PGS001824 and PGS002032 have identical partial-r (0.0716) and covariates; with no other differentiating evidence, PGS001824 is selected conservatively as the simpler penalized-regression model with far fewer variants.

Among the fixed candidates, PGS002786 is the only one whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches bipolar disorder (the others are bipolar I/II subtypes). However, all three records have endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (cognition/behavior traits rather than bipolar diagnosis) and report only small partial R² with basic covariates (age, PCs), with no PRS-only AUC/R², so the direct-match evidence is limited.

PGS001033 is the only candidate whose trait_efo directly matches the target (blood coagulation disease) and it reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.634; PGS R2 0.0578) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array). The other two scores target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO and provide only partial-correlation metrics, making them less directly aligned and less comparable on PRS discrimination.

PGS001336 is a direct-match breast carcinoma score that reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.596 and PGS R2 0.016 with no covariates) in a large European validation (n=67,425), making it more comparable than candidates reporting only covariate-inflated full-model AUCs. Many alternatives either lack PRS-only metrics, use heavy clinical risk-model covariates (e.g., BCSC/Rosner-Colditz), or target subtypes/special populations; while some have larger validation N, their reported metrics are full-model only and thus less informative for standalone PGS quality.

All candidates are direct matches to celiac disease, but PGS001301 is the only one reporting clearly PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.8287; PGS R² 0.1422) with basic covariates and a very large training set (n=269,704) plus multi-ancestry evaluation. Its PRS-only R² is plausible relative to EUR h2 estimates for celiac disease (liability h2 ~0.15–0.45), whereas several alternatives report only full-model AUROC or partial-r, making PRS discrimination less comparable.

All candidates are direct matches for cervical carcinoma, but only PGS001299 reports PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.552 and PGS R2 0.00263) alongside training size (n=269,704), making its predictive evidence interpretable without relying on covariate-boosted full-model metrics. Competing scores mainly report full-model C-index/AUROC with additional epidemiologic covariates (e.g., parity, oral contraceptive use, smoking), which are not comparable to standalone PRS performance; their HR per SD (~1.2–1.33) suggests only modest signal. PGS001299 therefore has the cleanest, most directly comparable PRS evidence among the fixed candidates.

PGS001174 is a direct cholelithiasis score with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC 0.623 and PGS R² 0.028) under basic covariates, enabling the cleanest cross-candidate comparison; its PRS-only R² is plausible relative to EUR h2 estimates for ICD10 K80 (~0.013–0.029 observed scale). Other direct-label candidates (PGS004476/PGS004546/PGS005150) lack comparable discrimination metrics and have unknown or minimal reporting, while the portability-study scores (PGS001861/PGS002072) target a broader combined endpoint and report only partial correlation, making them less directly comparable for cholelithiasis.

PGS004158 is a direct CKD score with a clean evaluation setup (covariates=0) and the strongest reported discrimination among the comparable no-covariate family (full-model AUROC 0.592, R² 0.020) in a large validation (n=90,274) with EUR/SAS evaluation. Competing direct-match candidates either lack PRS-comparable metrics and/or use heavy clinical covariate packaging (e.g., PGS002237, PGS004889) or show much weaker PRS-only performance (e.g., PGS001272 PGS-only AUROC 0.536, R² 0.002). The observed R² (~0.02) is plausible relative to CKD h2 estimates (~0.01–0.02 observed scale), supporting that the signal is not obviously covariate-inflated.

Among direct COPD candidates, PGS001783 reports the strongest PRS-comparable signal (Nagelkerke R² with covariates regressed out = 0.038) and is trained on a large multi-biobank GWAS with some non-EUR contribution, supporting robustness/portability. Competing UKB-only snpnet COPD scores have much weaker PGS-only metrics (R² ~0.002–0.003; AUROC ~0.54–0.55), and the J44 2024 scores report only ORs (1.31–1.49) without discrimination metrics and with unknown covariates, lowering confidence despite reasonable effect sizes.

PGS004621 is a direct match to the target (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both cirrhosis) and is built with a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (~1.09M) and exceptionally large multi-cohort European evaluation (n≈1,153,995) using only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). Competing direct-match scores are sparse GWS-variant sets (PGS000726: 12 variants; PGS000776: 9 variants with a more restricted/at-risk incident endpoint) or have much smaller/less clear evaluation (e.g., PGS001777 n=1,390 with unknown covariates), while alcohol-specific scores (PGS000704/PGS004913/PGS001777) are less aligned to generic cirrhosis of liver.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are direct matches (same reported phenotype/EFO), same UKB training (n=391,124), same evaluation setting and covariates, and show essentially identical partial correlation (~0.056), so performance does not differentiate. Given this tie, the LDpred2 model PGS002034 is preferred on structural grounds because it uses far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally a positive within-family signal for capturing polygenic signal when other metadata are comparable; however, the absence of PRS-only AUC/R² keeps overall quality assessment sub-optimal.

Both candidates directly match corneal dystrophy and come from the same UKB portability study with similar covariates and validation (European n=19,321), so the main differentiators are structural/performance signals. PGS002042 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (59,944 vs 38) and shows a higher partial correlation in the selected European validation record (0.0471 vs 0.0384), supporting stronger polygenic signal capture. Heritability records were unavailable for additional ceiling-based sanity checking, so confidence is moderate.

PGS003725 is a direct-match CAD score with a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2), substantial training size (n=116,649), and broad multi-ancestry evaluation (n=308,264) with only basic covariate adjustment (age/sex/PCs), supporting portability and reducing packaging concerns. Several alternatives report only full-model AUCs (often covariate-inflated) or have narrower/special-population endpoints, while PGS003725 also shows strong per-SD effect sizes (OR 2.14; HR 1.75), consistent with meaningful PRS signal.

All candidates are direct matches for Crohn’s disease, but PGS001331 provides explicit PRS-only metrics with basic covariates and slightly better PRS-only AUROC/R² than PGS001330 in the same UKB/snpnet study family. PGS004254 reports only a full-model AUROC (no PRS-only metric), making its apparent performance less comparable despite a larger variant count; the PRS-only evidence is cleaner for PGS001331.

For the target trait dementia, PGS000929 is a direct-match (trait_efo=dementia; phenotyping_reported all-cause dementia) and is one of the few candidates reporting PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.627 and PGS-only R² 0.023) rather than only covariate-boosted full-model metrics or effect sizes. It is trained at large scale (n=269,704) and evaluated in a large validation set (n=67,425) with multi-ancestry evaluation, while using only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its reported incremental AUROC (0.0229) interpretable as PRS contribution.

Among direct-match depressive-disorder candidates, PGS002036 has strong structural support: large UKB training sample (n=391,124), a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2) with substantial variant coverage (807,338), and multi-ancestry evaluation context, whereas many alternatives report only full-model metrics or have endpoint mismatches (e.g., medication side-effect, brain imaging). Reported performance is not PRS-only for most candidates, but PGS002036 shows the best available PRS-isolated signal (partial-r=0.0556) with basic covariates, making it the most defensible choice despite limited comparable AUC/R² reporting.

All candidates are direct matches for dilated cardiomyopathy; among those with explicit PRS-only discrimination, PGS004949 shows the strongest univariate (PRS-only) AUC (0.68) and highest per-SD OR (1.91) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). Competing 2024-04 scores (PGS004861/PGS004862) report only full-model AUROC/R² (no PRS-only metric), making them less comparable for PRS ranking despite larger validation N. The reported PRS-only delta liability-scale R² (0.095) is below the available cardiomyopathy liability h2 estimates, supporting metric plausibility.

All candidates are direct matches, but PGS000997 provides the cleanest PRS-comparable evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.591 and PGS-only R²=0.0178 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), and its PRS-only R² is plausible relative to diverticular disease h² estimates (~0.01–0.03 observed in UKB LDSC). PGS000996 has materially weaker PRS-only metrics, while PGS004474/PGS004544 lack comparable discrimination metrics and PGS004614 reports only a covariate-augmented full-model AUROC (includes family history), making its PRS contribution unclear.

All candidates are direct matches to Dupuytren contracture, but PGS001254 is the only one reporting explicit PRS-only discrimination/variance metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6646; PGS R2 0.0247) with basic covariates, enabling a cleaner like-for-like assessment. PGS001880 and PGS002092 come from a portability framework and report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUC/R2), making their predictive evidence less directly comparable despite larger variant counts and multi-ancestry evaluation.

All candidates map to follicular lymphoma via trait_efo, but only PGS002304 has a clean follicular-lymphoma phenotyping label; its validation N is very small (n=197) and covariates are unknown. Between the two higher-capacity PRSweb models with basic covariates and larger validation (n=3,256), PGS000644 (lassosum; 2.2M variants) shows slightly better full-model AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532) and higher pseudo-R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282) than PGS000643, though both lack PRS-only metrics, keeping overall quality sub-optimal.

PGS001792 targets a direct clinical endpoint (primary open-angle glaucoma) and uses a methodologically strong genome-wide Bayesian approach (PRS-CS-auto) with very large external validation (n=347,396) and a PRS-comparable metric reported as covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.032. Competing exact-label glaucoma scores from pan-trait/portability frameworks either show only modest PRS-only AUC/R2 (e.g., snpnet AUC~0.60; partial-r~0.046) or lack PRS-only metrics, while PGS001792’s covariate set is basic (age/sex/PCs) and its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to glaucoma h2 estimates.

Among direct gout scores, PGS001248 provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.669 and PGS R2 0.040 with no covariates) on a large UKB training set (n=269,704) and sizable validation (n=67,425), making it the cleanest comparable evidence in the list. Several alternatives report only full-model AUROC (often covariate-adjusted) or effect sizes without PRS-only metrics, which are less comparable for ranking; PGS001248’s PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to available gout heritability estimates.

All candidates are direct matches (trait_efo Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; phenotyping lymphocytic thyroiditis) and share the same evaluation setting with only full-model AUROC reported and covariates unknown, so performance is not cleanly PRS-comparable. Given that, PGS005271 is preferred for stronger structural signals (PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) among the set, while small full-model AUROC differences are not decisive.

PGS001790 is a direct heart-failure endpoint and is the only candidate reporting a PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R²=0.006981) alongside evaluation in a very large European validation sample (n=358,905) with only basic demographic/PC covariates. Many other direct-label candidates report only full-model AUC/C-index or effect sizes with unknown covariates, making their discrimination evidence less comparable; the UKB portability-framework CHF scores report only partial correlations in small validation sets (~20k).

All candidates are direct matches for hip osteoarthritis, but PGS002763 has the strongest standalone PRS evidence: an OR per SD of 1.38 (n=39,444) using a genome-wide PRS-CS model (~1.05M variants), which is typically more informative than sparse genome-wide-significant scores with limited metrics. PGS000967 is the only one with explicit PGS-only AUC/R2, but its PRS-only signal is weak (AUROC 0.561; R2 0.0063) relative to the trait’s moderate heritability estimates (~0.19–0.26), suggesting limited discriminative power despite large UKB training. Other recent models either lack comparable PRS-only metrics and show smaller effect sizes (e.g., OR~1.22–1.30) or rely on proxy endpoints like total hip replacement.

Direct-match Hodgkin’s lymphoma candidates are present (PGS000637/638/639/640 and PGS003449), but only the PRSweb set reports discrimination and all are based on a very small training sample (n=736) with small validation (n=775) and only full-model AUROC reported. Within that direct-match cluster, PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) shows the strongest reported performance (full-model AUROC 0.62; highest pseudo-R² 0.0276; OR 1.48) with standard covariates (age/sex/PCs), making it the best-supported option despite limited evidence.

PGS001320 is a direct-match hypertension score with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC 0.629 and PGS R2 0.0649 without covariates) using basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and large UKB training (n=269,704) with multi-ancestry evaluation. Competing direct-match hypertension candidates mostly report only full-model AUROC or incremental/partial-correlation metrics, making PRS-only comparability weaker; PGS001320’s PRS-only R2 is also well below hypertension h2 estimates (~0.13), supporting metric plausibility.

PGS001042 is a direct-match hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoint with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6339; PGS R² 0.0236) evaluated with only basic covariates, making it the cleanest comparable performance evidence in the candidate set. It slightly outperforms the near-identical sibling PGS001043 on PRS-only AUROC/R² and has a larger variant set (226 vs 69). Other candidates either lack PRS-only discrimination metrics (partial-r only) or report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (Graves’ disease scores), reducing comparability despite larger multi-ancestry context.

PGS004911 has a direct hypertrophic cardiomyopathy endpoint (phenotyping_reported matches the target), uses a modern genome-wide PRS-CS model with ~374k variants, and is evaluated in a large European validation sample (n=343,182) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Within the same 2025 study family it shows stronger reported discrimination than the non-MTAG sibling (full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031) while avoiding the heavy clinical/rare-variant covariate packaging seen in PGS000739, whose high AUROC is likely covariate-driven and not PRS-comparable.

PGS000965 has a direct hypothyroidism/myxoedema endpoint and uniquely reports PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.689; PGS R² 0.0727) in a large European validation (n=67,425) with basic covariates, making it the cleanest comparable evidence among candidates. Several alternatives either target therapy-induced hypothyroidism, report only full-model/incremental metrics (often with heavier or unknown covariates), or lack PRS-only metrics entirely; PGS001181 is very close but uses a time-to-event ‘other hypothyroidism’ endpoint.

Both candidates directly match the target endpoint (Disorders of iron metabolism; EFO iron metabolism disease) with identical training (UKB EUR n=391,124), validation (EUR n=19,883), and basic covariates, so the main differentiators are method and PRS signal. PGS002031 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (6,713 vs 654) and shows slightly higher partial correlation in European validation (0.1355 vs 0.1307), consistent with stronger genome-wide shrinkage capture; the reported partial-r is also plausible relative to available h2 estimates (~0.04–0.09 for related iron traits).

PGS000114 is the only candidate that directly targets juvenile idiopathic arthritis at the overall disease level (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align), whereas the others are subtype-specific. All candidates report only full-model AUROC with the same light covariates (sex, PCs), so performance is not cleanly PRS-only comparable; given that, the direct endpoint fidelity makes PGS000114 the best-supported choice despite some subtypes showing higher full-model AUROC.

PGS004908 is a direct match to kidney cancer (phenotyping_reported: kidney cancer) and is supported by a recent large multi-ancestry GWAS with a substantially larger variant set (107) than other GWS-hit scores, plus strong effect-size evidence (OR 1.5 per SD) and the highest reported AUROC (0.74), albeit as a covariate-adjusted full-model metric. Competing direct-match candidates either lack comparable discrimination metrics (PGS000161/PGS004245/PGS003744), have much weaker full-model AUROC (~0.56–0.57; PGS000722/PGS004690), or are UKB-only small-development scores with modest AUROC (~0.52; PGS000605/PGS000606).

For the target kidney failure, the direct-match candidates are PGS000708 (diabetic kidney failure) and the N18 chronic renal failure scores (PGS004492/PGS004562). PGS004562 is the most endpoint-aligned (N18 chronic renal failure/kidney failure) without the diabetic-subtype restriction, and it shows the strongest per-SD effect size among the direct matches (OR≈1.40 vs OR≈1.17 for PGS004492 and HR≈1.19 for PGS000708), though confidence is limited because no PRS-only AUC/R² and covariates are reported for the N18 models.

PGS001192 is a direct knee osteoarthritis/gonarthrosis endpoint and is the only candidate reporting explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.5566; PGS R2 0.0068) with basic covariates, enabling a cleaner cross-model comparison; its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to knee OA h2 (~0.21). Other direct-match candidates mostly lack PRS-only metrics and report only full-model AUC or per-SD OR/HR, making them harder to rank reliably despite larger variant counts.

All candidates map to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, but none reports a clean PRS-only AUROC/R²; the most interpretable PRS evidence is per-SD effect size. PGS000054 (21 genome-wide significant variants) reports a strong OR=1.73 per SD in validation (AMR; n=3,324) with only basic covariates (age, sex), whereas PGS000053’s OR is more modest (1.29) and other candidates report only full-model R²/AUROC with unknown covariates or non-disease endpoints.

PGS000078 is a direct lung-cancer PRS with large EUR evaluation (n=392,539) and a coherent multi-cohort training set; its reported HR per SD (1.16) supports non-trivial PRS signal. Many other candidates either target restricted endpoints (e.g., early-onset or never-smokers), have much smaller validation, or report only covariate-heavy full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics; PGS000078 and its derivative PGS000789 share the same covariate-heavy evaluation, but PGS000078 is the original score rather than an inverse-weight reparameterization.

For the target lupus erythematosus, PGS002082 is the best-supported direct-match: it aligns to the umbrella phenotype (“Lupus (localized and systemic)”), is trained at very large scale (UKB n=391,124), uses a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2) with dense variant coverage (361,553), and is evaluated across multiple ancestry groups, supporting portability. Most SLE-labeled alternatives either target restricted sub-phenotypes (e.g., nephritis/renal disease, early-onset) or report only full-model AUROC with unknown/heavy covariates (e.g., phenotype risk score), making their discrimination evidence less comparable to a standalone PGS.

PGS000077 is a direct match to the target (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; phenotyping_reported=Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) with clean, basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) and large European validation (n=391,338). Competing direct-match lymphoid-leukemia scores either have very small validation (PGS000645 n=957; PGS002305 n=265) or are chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia subtype scores; and PGS000788’s higher full-model AUROC/R² is not PRS-only and appears inconsistent with the low h2 ceiling, making it less reliable for ranking.

PGS004606 is a direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: age-related macular degeneration) from a recent disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context, using a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (~1.0M) and a large European validation sample (n=163,011). Competing UKB portability/framework scores either show weak PRS-only discrimination (PGS001013 PGS-only AUROC 0.553; R² 0.006, consistent with low UKB self-report h2) or report only small partial correlations (PGS001834/PGS002041), while PGS004952’s very high AUROC appears to be full-model only and is based on a small validation set (n=1,232), making it less reliable for PRS-only ranking.

PGS001304 is a direct melanoma score with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.5909; PGS R2 0.01149) and multi-ancestry evaluation, making it the most comparable standalone-PRS option in this list. Many other melanoma-labeled candidates report only full-model AUROC and often include substantial non-genetic risk-factor covariates (e.g., UV/tanning/phenotype/family history), which limits comparability to a pure PGS; the PRS-only R2 for PGS001304 is also plausible relative to melanoma h2_liability (~0.08–0.25 in EUR).

All candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS003450 has an endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (chronic lymphocytic leukemia). Among the remaining direct multiple-myeloma endpoints, PGS002281 shows the strongest validation discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.644 with basic covariates age/sex/region) and a strong risk gradient (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles) on a reasonable validation size (n=2,395), whereas the PRSweb scores have notably lower AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and PGS002306’s higher AUROC is based on a much smaller validation (n=290) with unknown covariates.

All candidates are direct matches for multiple sclerosis, but PGS001270 is the only one with explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.6586; PGS R² 0.0290) reported with basic covariates, enabling clean cross-model comparison. Alternatives either report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000809/PGS002726/PGS004699) or only partial correlation without PRS-only AUC/R² (PGS001831/PGS002038), making their apparent performance less attributable to the PGS itself despite some having larger variant counts or higher full-model AUROC.

Among direct myocardial infarction candidates, PGS001317 reports the strongest PRS-only discrimination (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.6006; PGS R2 0.0165) with basic covariates and a large UKB training set, while other MI scores have slightly lower PRS-only AUROC/R2 or lack PRS-only metrics. Its PRS-only R2 is consistent with MI heritability estimates (observed h2 ~0.007–0.034), supporting that the signal is plausible rather than covariate-driven.

Both candidates are direct matches to J33/Nasal cavity polyp with identical UKB EUR training (n=174,489), EUR validation (n=56,192), and variant count (~1.06M), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only per-SD OR). Given otherwise matched metadata within the same publication family, PGS004535 is preferred because it shows a stronger reported effect size (OR 1.60 vs 1.35), indicating stronger PRS discriminative signal.

Both candidates are direct matches (tobacco use disorder; EFO nicotine dependence) from the same UKB portability study with similar covariates and validation N, so the main differentiator is PRS performance: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557) in the selected European validation record. It also uses a genome-wide LDpred2 model with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a supportive signal when endpoints and study context are otherwise matched.

PGS001814 is a direct endpoint match to nodular goiter (phenotyping_reported: nontoxic multinodular goiter) with clean, basic covariates and explicit PRS-only-style evaluation (partial correlation adjusted for age/sex/PCs) plus multi-ancestry portability evaluation. Competing benign nodular goiter scores report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (not PRS-comparable), and the thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter scores are not aligned to the target endpoint.

PGS001298 is a direct obesity endpoint score with the cleanest, explicitly reported PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.5757; PGS R² 0.0115) using only basic covariates, and it is trained at large scale in UKB (n=269,704) with multi-ancestry evaluation available. Most other direct-match candidates either lack PRS-comparable metrics entirely (only OR/beta or full-model R² with unknown covariates) or use broader administrative phenotype bundles, making their standalone PRS performance harder to judge from the visible metadata.

PGS001274 is a direct-match osteoporosis score with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC 0.57595; PGS R2 0.00945) under basic covariates, and it modestly outperforms the closest sibling PGS001273 on PRS-only metrics. Its PRS-only R2 is below available EUR h2 estimates for osteoporosis (liability h2 ~0.05–0.18 depending on definition), supporting that the signal is plausible and not obviously covariate-driven; many other candidates lack PRS-only metrics or have unknown covariates, making them harder to rank confidently despite larger variant counts or OR-only reporting.

Both candidates directly target otosclerosis, but PGS001255 provides explicit PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.6319; PGS R² 0.01341) with only basic covariates and a larger European validation sample (n=67,425). PGS002046 reports only a partial correlation (0.0182) without PRS-only AUROC/R², making cross-model performance comparison less direct despite its larger variant count and training N.

PGS000082 is a direct ovarian cancer endpoint (incident ovarian cancer) with very large European validation (n=211,958) and a disease-focused multi-cohort context; among broadly aligned candidates it shows the strongest reported discrimination (full-model AUROC/C-index ~0.656) without being restricted to BRCA carriers or a narrow subtype. Many ovarian-neoplasm-labeled PRSweb scores have much smaller training/validation and weaker full-model AUROC (~0.52–0.57), and several other candidates are BRCA-carrier-specific or subtype-specific, reducing generalizability to the generic ovarian neoplasm target.

All candidates are direct matches for pancreatic cancer/carcinoma, but most report only covariate-inflated full-model AUROC (often with family history/clinical risk factors or horizon/age conditioning), making PRS quality hard to compare. PGS000385 provides the cleanest, most PRS-informative evidence: a UKB-developed EUR score with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and multiple PRS-linked metrics (OR per SD 1.384; top 1% vs rest OR 2.58; pseudo-R² 0.019), whereas the very high AUROC in PGS002264 is likely driven by diabetes/clinical-risk packaging. Given pancreatic cancer’s modest h2 (~0.06 observed), PGS000385’s modest R² is plausible and interpretable.

PGS000903 is a direct Parkinson’s disease endpoint score trained at very large scale (n=1,473,098) with broad variant coverage (1,805; C+T) and multi-ancestry evaluation, and it reports the strongest available genetic-performance evidence in this set (R²=0.054 and OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25). Competing candidates either target progression/dementia endpoints, have far fewer variants, or report only full-model AUROC with heavier covariate packaging (e.g., family history), making their discrimination less PRS-comparable.

PGS002055 is a direct match to peripheral vascular disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported) and, among the two like-for-like UKB portability scores, shows slightly higher PRS signal (partial-r 0.0175 vs 0.0151) with the same clean/basic covariate adjustment and identical training/validation context. The PAD-focused alternatives are either heavily covariate-packaged in a restricted T2D setting (PGS005158) or report only full-model C-index without PRS-only metrics (PGS005217), making them less comparable for standalone PGS selection for the target trait.

PGS003586 is a direct-match preeclampsia score (trait_reported and trait_efo align) from a large multi-cohort GWAS/training set (n=212,034) using PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants and clean/basic covariates (maternal age, age^2, PCs). Among candidates lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, it shows the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20 for the sibling score) and has clearer endpoint alignment than PGS004593, whose phenotyping_reported is gestational hypertension and lacks training-sample metadata despite a larger validation N.

PGS001291 is a direct prostate cancer score with the strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the list: it reports PGS-only AUROC (0.654) and PGS-only R² (0.0316) in European validation, unlike most candidates that report only covariate-inflated full-model metrics. Its very large training sample (n=269,704) also supports robustness; the reported PGS-only R² is well below available prostate-cancer h² liability estimates, consistent with a plausible PRS signal.

PGS001312 is the cleanest direct-match to the target (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported both psoriasis) and reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.692; PGS R2 0.052) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) in a large UKB development set (n=269,704) and sizable European validation (n=67,425). Competing direct-match psoriasis scores either lack PRS-only metrics (many report only partial-r or incremental R2) or target severity/time-to-event endpoints, making their performance less comparable for generic psoriasis risk.

Both candidates align to psoriatic arthritis/arthropathy, but PGS001287 provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.676; PGS R² 0.0335) with basic covariates and large EUR training (n=269,704) plus multi-ancestry evaluation, whereas PGS000342 reports only a modest full-model AUROC (0.562) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metric. Heritability lookup did not return a direct psoriatic-arthritis h2 estimate, but the available PRS-only R² for PGS001287 is in a plausible range for complex disease and is the cleanest comparable evidence in this candidate set.

PGS001280 is a direct-match pulmonary embolism score (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported: PE/TTE PE) with explicit PRS-only performance reported using only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and large UKB training (n≈269k). Its PRS-only AUROC (0.6077) and PGS R2 (0.0140) are competitive and broadly consistent with available PE heritability ceilings, while other direct-match candidates either mix PE with DVT, use broader self-report composites, or lack PRS-only metrics / have unknown covariates.

PGS001030 is the only candidate that directly matches the target label/endpoint (“Pulmonary fibrosis”) and it reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6252; PGS R2 0.0142) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array). The alternative idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis scores are subtype matches: PGS001791 has a much lower PRS-comparable R2 (0.005929) and no PGS-only AUROC, while PGS004695 lacks comparable discrimination metrics (only a quintile HR).

All candidates are direct matches, but PGS001137 has the cleanest endpoint alignment to the target (“Retinal detachment”) and reports explicit PRS-only metrics with basic covariates; it also shows higher PRS-only AUROC (0.573) and R² (0.0066) than the closely related TTE composite PGS000990. The portability-study scores (PGS001833/PGS002040) have larger training N but only partial-correlation metrics, making them harder to compare directly against the PRS-only AUC/R² evidence; the chosen PRS-only R² remains plausible relative to low observed h2 estimates for similar UKB retinal detachment phenotypes.

PGS001310 is the cleanest direct-match for rheumatoid arthritis with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC no covariates ~0.60; PGS R2 ~0.015) and basic covariates only, plus large UKB training (n=269,704) and multi-ancestry evaluation. Many other RA-labeled candidates report only full-model metrics or effect sizes with heavier/unclear packaging, or target narrower endpoints (e.g., seropositive/time-to-event), making them less comparable for generic RA risk.

PGS000922 is a direct sarcoidosis endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported align) with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.6428; PGS R2 no covariates=0.0174) evaluated with basic covariates only, making it the cleanest comparable evidence in this set. PGS000923 is time-to-event (a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty) with only marginally higher PRS-only AUROC/R2, while PGS001872/PGS002084 have weaker/less comparable performance reporting (partial correlation only) and their trait_efo points to skin sarcoidosis rather than sarcoidosis broadly.

All four PGS000133–PGS000136 are direct schizophrenia endpoints with similar basic covariates; none reports PRS-only AUC/R², so full-model AUROC is only weakly comparable. PGS000136 has a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.7) with a reasonably large European validation sample (n=18,461), whereas PGS000135’s higher AUROC (0.74) comes from a much smaller validation (n=9,569) and lacks an effect-size cross-check. PGS002785 is not endpoint-aligned (phenotyping is cognitive function), so it is not preferred for schizophrenia risk prediction.

All candidates are direct matches (same reported trait/EFO), same study family, EUR-only training/evaluation, and use only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), so full-model AUROC is reasonably comparable across them. PGS000471 shows the strongest validation performance signals (highest AUROC 0.569, highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0255, and strongest OR per SD 1.40 and top-1% OR 3.77) versus PGS000470 and PGS000469. Although metrics are full-model (no PGS-only AUC/R²) and the trait’s estimated h2 is low/uncertain, within-family evidence consistently favors PGS000471.

Across candidates, only obstructive sleep apnea scores show materially stronger association evidence (e.g., OR per SD 1.53 for PGS005220) and higher reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.79) than the ExPRSweb sleep-apnea scores whose full-model AUROCs cluster near 0.49–0.53 with near-null ORs. Although PGS005220’s AUROC is covariate-influenced (includes BMI) and no PGS-only metrics are reported, it has a coherent OSA endpoint and stronger effect-size signal than alternatives; between the two 2025 OSA scores, the unadjusted-BMI version is less phenotype-conditioned than the AdjustedBMI score.

PGS000461 is a direct endpoint match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all squamous cell carcinoma) with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs) and shows the strongest effect-size evidence among the direct-match set (OR per SD 1.49; top 1% vs rest OR 3.51) alongside the highest reported AUROC (0.599) within the same evaluation setting. Competing SCC scores trained in UKB have much larger training/validation N but weaker reported discrimination/effect sizes (AUROC ~0.57–0.575; OR ~1.32–1.33), and PGS005209 is a survivorship/radiation-exposure-specific endpoint rather than generic SCC risk.
No candidate PGS models were provided in the fixed candidate list, so no direct-match PGS can be selected for the target trait (testicular carcinoma).

All candidates are direct matches for thyroid carcinoma, but most report only full-model AUROC (often with additional covariates) and lack PRS-only metrics. PGS001289 uniquely provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.618 and PGS R2 0.01236 with no covariates) from a large EUR training set (n=269,704) and multi-ancestry evaluation, making its predictive evidence most comparable and least dependent on covariate packaging among the options.

PGS001297 is a direct type 1 diabetes score with explicit PRS-only performance reported (PGS AUROC 0.771 and PGS R² 0.0912) using only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large training sample (n=269,704). Many other direct-match candidates report only full-model AUROC with unknown/heavier covariates (e.g., PGS000021 includes autoantibody status/BMI) or lack PRS-only metrics entirely, making their discrimination less comparable to a standalone PGS.

PGS001294 is a direct-match T2D endpoint (non-insulin-dependent diabetes) and is one of the few candidates reporting PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.636; PGS R2 0.034), enabling cleaner cross-model comparison than candidates reporting only covariate-inflated full-model AUC/C-index. Its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to EUR T2D heritability estimates (~0.07–0.15 observed; ~0.09–0.17 liability), supporting that the signal is genuinely polygenic rather than purely covariate-driven.

All candidates are direct matches for ulcerative colitis, but PGS001306 provides the cleanest PRS-comparable evidence with explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.630) and PGS-only R² (0.020) under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). Competing scores either use a time-to-event endpoint (PGS001307), lack PRS-only metrics (PGS001855/PGS002066/PGS004253), have unknown covariates (PGS002066), or report only full-model AUROC/effect sizes that are not directly comparable to standalone PRS performance (PGS004253). The reported PGS-only R² is well below ulcerative colitis h2 estimates (~0.21–0.24), supporting metric plausibility.

All candidates are direct matches for bladder cancer, but most report only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only). Within the Cancer PRSweb family with comparable basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), PGS000611 shows among the strongest effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.284) plus a strong top-1% vs rest OR (2.66) and is trained/evaluated in a larger UKB-based setting (samples_training 12,992; validation n=13,530) than the MGI-based siblings. Very high full-model AUROCs in PGS000071/PGS000782 are likely dominated by non-genetic covariates (age, smoking, BMI), making them less informative for selecting the best standalone PGS.

All candidates are direct matches to urolithiasis/nephrolithiasis; among those with comparable endpoints, PGS002075 shows the strongest reported PRS signal via the highest partial correlation (0.0385 vs 0.0323) in the same portability study family with identical covariates and training design. It also uses LDpred2 with very large variant coverage (731,196) and large EUR training (n=391,124) with multi-ancestry evaluation, whereas the 2024 models report only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) and PGS001250 has lower training N and smaller variant count with weaker PRS-only metrics (AUROC 0.5668; R2 0.0059).

PGS001795 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/phenotyping_reported directly matches the target (uterine cancer) and it uses a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (911,692) and multi-biobank development context. Its reported PRS-only metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.001948) provides a cleaner PRS-comparable signal than candidates reporting only covariate-inflated full-model AUROC, and it remains well below the available h2 ceiling estimates for related uterine/endometrial cancer self-report.

PGS001536 has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence for vitiligo, reporting PGS-only AUROC=0.64193 and PGS-only R²=0.01621 in a large European validation (n=67,425) with only basic covariates; its PRS-only R² is well below vitiligo h² (~0.17–0.26), supporting plausibility. The other candidates either have endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported (red hair; anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism) and/or lack comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics.
